children.text: Participants
Gvern: Varun, Sriharsha
ThinkByte: Raghu Gorrela, Harsha Thota, Bharath MVS
Key Takeaways
The meeting focused on developing an AI operating system to optimize GMP operations in the life sciences sector.
Attendees included representatives from Gvern.ai and Thinkbyte.ai, discussing collaboration opportunities and product development.
Issues addressed included digitizing compliance processes, integrating systems for seamless operation, and targeting tier-two companies for cost-effective solutions.
Planned actions involve finalizing product features, setting pricing strategies, and scheduling follow-up meetings to solidify partnerships.
The team aims to create a unified, AI-driven platform to enhance manufacturing efficiency and compliance, targeting smaller life sciences companies.
Action Items
Suggested that Raghu consider a medical loan for their customer, emphasizing the importance of understanding the bottom line and being open to any use case.
Bharath MVS
Schedule a meeting with Sriharsha to discuss product development, compliance requirements, and pricing.
Talk to Harsha and express willingness to collaborate on building the product together, focusing on the entire product and a separate module for audit certifications.
Schedule another call to discuss setting a new standard for the AI market and determining a fee of 50 lakh rupees per facility.
Varun
Gather and document compliance and audit requirements.
Positive Moments
Excited about the AI-powered platform for GMP operations.
We're exploring a 50/50 revenue split model.
Partnering with distribution partners is a great move.
Highlighting specific use cases for clarity.
Business Goals
Streamline GMP operations with AI platforms.
Focus on manufacturing, quality, and laboratory processes.
Leverage AI to automate workflows and improve efficiency.
Enhance batch management and SOP compliance.
Integrate systems for seamless operations across the board.
Impact
Leverages AI to optimize workflows and decision-making.
Reduced manual tasks, leading to increased efficiency.
Streamlined audit processes and compliance management.
Enhanced automation in quality control and documentation.
Improved production scheduling and resource allocation.
Current Workflow
No-code workflow builder for custom processes.
Batch manufacturing recorder logs raw materials, batch size, etc.
Trackwise for QA requests and control copies.
Integrates with AI agents to streamline workflow execution.
Workflow begins with order confirmation and production planning.
Features Interested
Automates workflow execution and batch management.
Interested in AI-driven compliance for manufacturing and quality.
Significantly simplifies audit processes.
Focused on AI-driven batch management, quality management, and training management solutions.
Pain Points
Must quickly identify deviations and corrective actions, especially in temperature control.
Manual processes are costly and inefficient.
Documentation and compliance need automation and digitization.
Customer difficulties have caused physical gauges on the needle to move, which are not digital and are of the meter type, specifically the Atlantic gauges.
Had to solve manufacturing quality and document management to achieve continuous audit readiness.
Price discovery for software market requires live customer data points to determine ROI and effort accurately.
Compliance documentation is time-consuming and needs automation.
Competitors
Existing solution is a paper-based batch manufacturing record document, 100 pages long.
Current Solution: EBMR (Electronic Batch Manufacturing Record)
The prospect wants to replace EBMR with a more streamlined MES solution.
Prospects are actively looking for a modern MES solution that ensures compliance and efficiency.
Highly expensive and error-prone due to manual entries.
Pricing
Target smaller companies that can't afford million-dollar solutions.
Flexibility is key to adapt to client needs.
Skepticism on pricing models, especially modules from Databricks.
Pain Points about pricing fairness and market competitiveness.
Pricing strategy should be around $250,000.
Budget
Targeting 1/10th the price of big players like Honeywell.
Pricing strategy should reflect value delivered.
One-off cost for licensing; 20% recurring costs.
Budget range: $100,000 to $150,000.
Decision Process
Financial considerations: Allocate $100,000 to $150,000.
Involve design partners early in the process to refine use cases.
Emphasize real-time audit readiness and compliance.
Customizability and integration are key features.
Streamline solutions to enhance quality management and documentation.
Timeline
Need a tool that ensures 100% audit pass rate tomorrow.
